title: Milliseconds to Magic: Real‑Time Workflows using the Gemini Live API and Pipecat
talk_summary: A Gemini Live API + Pipecat demo talk about building real-time voice agents, showing a live (buggy) demo of a voice-driven list/app manager and discussing the voice AI stack layers. It is almost entirely about speech interfaces and multimodal latency, not about agent orchestration, review, or model cost.

takeaways.technique: Minimal tool scaffolding, let model infer usage
takeaways.what_they_do: They expose a function (add text to screen with optional clear arg) with essentially no instructions on when to use it, and rely on the LLM to infer correct usage from context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: basically no instructions to the LLM about how to display text on the screen and just telling it it has a function

takeaways.technique: Live adversarial demo as informal eval
takeaways.what_they_do: They ran the bleeding-edge build live with a second person probing it, surfacing failures (turn detection, name spelling, list duplication) to discuss where bugs live in the stack.
takeaways.evidence_quote: fire up a version of this code, have Shista talk to it, and see what breaks

takeaways.what_they_do: They observe that hard problems first solved in app code get absorbed into frameworks then APIs/models, so you should avoid over-building app-level logic that will be commoditized.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the capabilities tend to move down the stack
